name: json2video
description: Create and render videos with JSON2Video: templates, AI voiceovers, subtitles and AI images.

interface.longDescription:
Create and render videos in your JSON2Video account without leaving the chat.

Describe the video you want, or pick one of the featured templates, and JSON2Video renders it as an MP4 and returns the link. Videos can combine text, images, video clips, AI voiceovers, subtitles, music and AI-generated images, in vertical (Reels, Shorts, TikTok), square or horizontal format.

What you can do:
- Render a video from a featured template or one of your own templates, filling its variables from your request.
- Build a custom video scene by scene, validate it and render it.
- Save a video design as a reusable template in your account.
- Check the status of renders and list your recent videos.
- Upload, list and manage files in your media library.
- See your remaining render credits.

JSON2Video only accesses the account you connect, and you can disconnect at any time from your JSON2Video dashboard.
capabilities: Preview templates and videos in chat
defaultPrompt: Make a 15-second vertical video announcing our new coffee shop.
Show me the featured video templates.
List my last 5 videos and their status.

positive.description: Render a video from a featured template
positive.prompt: Show me the featured JSON2Video templates, pick one that fits a shop opening, and render it with the text 'Grand opening this Saturday'.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists featured templates and shows the best matches as cards with their real thumbnails (show_templates), then, without waiting for another message, picks one, reads its variables (get_template) and renders it with the requested text (render_video; depending on the user's connector permission setting, ChatGPT may ask to allow it first). The finished MP4 is shown in a video player (show_video), or the project id and status if the render is still running.

positive.description: Build and render a custom video
positive.prompt: Create a 10-second vertical video with the text 'Summer Sale - 30% off' over this image: https://assets.json2video.com/assets/images/london-01.jpg
positive.expected_behavior: Builds a 1080x1920 movie JSON with the image and the text, usually validates it first, and renders it (render_video; depending on the user's connector permission setting, ChatGPT may ask to allow it first). The MP4 is shown in a video player (show_video), or the project id and status if the render is still running.

positive.description: List recent renders and check one
positive.prompt: List my last 5 JSON2Video renders and tell me the status of the newest one.
positive.tools_triggered: list_recent_renders, check_status (only if the list does not already include the status)
positive.expected_behavior: Returns up to 5 recent renders with project id, status and URL, and the current status of the newest render.

positive.prompt: How many render credits do I have left in JSON2Video?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the remaining credits and plan quotas of the connected account. Does not show offers or ask the user to upgrade.

positive.description: Upload a file to the media library
positive.prompt: Upload this image to my JSON2Video media library and then list the files there: https://assets.json2video.com/assets/images/london-01.jpg
positive.expected_behavior: Depending on the user's connector permission setting, ChatGPT may ask to allow media_upload first. The image is uploaded from the public URL and the stored file name and URL are confirmed. If a file with that name already exists, the new one is saved under a numbered name (london-01-2.jpg, london-01-3.jpg, ...) and the reply says so; an existing file is never overwritten. Then the media library is listed, including the new file.

negative.prompt: What's the weather in Barcelona tomorrow?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Render videos from templates or custom designs, preview templates and finished videos in chat, save templates, check render status, and manage the media library. Template renders now keep the template's default values for any variable the request does not set, and uploads never fail on an existing file name.
